links.name: OCuLink
links.lanes: PCIe 4.0 x4 (usually wired from an M.2 slot or a dedicated port)
links.measuredNotes: Measured ~6.6-6.7 GB/s in the TB5 comparison tests (gaming test, retailer blog). Cold-plug on most hosts (snippet). Per the Level1Techs thread, OCuLink worked on a GMKtec Evo-X2 via M.2.

links.name: USB4 v2 / Thunderbolt 5 (via DEG2)
links.lanes: Tunnelled PCIe; DEG2 capped at PCIe 4.0 x4 on both ports
links.measuredNotes: Headline 80 Gbps but the dock tops out at 64 Gbps PCIe; TB5 measured ~5.8 GB/s; gaming 14% slower than OCuLink on average.

links.name: USB4 40 Gbps
links.measuredNotes: Vendor/summary claim of ~32 Gbps usable PCIe (snippet only); not confirmed on an opened primary page.

links.name: PCIe slot (MS-S1 MAX)
links.measuredNotes: Internal x4 slot gives the same link width as OCuLink without a dock; the Framework Desktop slot is also x4 per the RDMA guide.

strixHaloResults.setup: RTX 5080 16GB via OCuLink on a Strix Halo mini PC (Vulkan, LM Studio)
strixHaloResults.result: About 3x the iGPU speed; drops to 1.6 tok/s when the model exceeds VRAM

strixHaloResults.setup: RTX Pro 6000 96GB via OCuLink + Strix Halo iGPU
strixHaloResults.workload: 32B dense and 122B MoE; split of 122B across both
strixHaloResults.result: 69 tok/s (32B); 121 tok/s (122B MoE); 37-38 tok/s when split across both; source says the OCuLink link bottlenecks the split

strixHaloResults.setup: Strix Halo + dGPU on Windows 11 Pro (forum reports)
strixHaloResults.result: Stability issues and 35-40% slowdowns reported; LM Studio 0.3.16 missed the iGPU when a dGPU was present; capping iGPU VRAM at 512MB in BIOS helped

docksAndAdapters.notes: Needs a separate ATX/SFX PSU. A search snippet showed other EU listings from EUR 90 to 129, not opened.

docksAndAdapters.name: Minisforum DEG2 (OCuLink + USB4 v2, M.2, 2.5G LAN)
docksAndAdapters.notes: No EUR price found on an opened page; snippets gave USD 259-299 and GBP 225. Gap.

docksAndAdapters.name: AOOSTAR AG02 (OCuLink + USB4, 800W PSU built in)
docksAndAdapters.notes: Snippet only: EUR 159.72 with coupon, EUR 164.04 listed, EUR 249 at Geekbuying. Merchant page not opened; unverified.

limits: Link is PCIe 4.0 x4 at best (~8 GB/s theoretical, ~6.6-6.7 GB/s measured), against Strix Halo unified memory; anything crossing the link is slow.
A model split across iGPU and eGPU is link-limited (MindStudio: 37-38 tok/s split vs 121 on the big GPU alone) and a model that overflows VRAM collapses (1.6 tok/s).
Cross-vendor split needs Vulkan; CUDA and ROCm do not interoperate (MindStudio).
BAR trouble with very large VRAM cards (RTX Pro 6000); 16-24GB cards were fine in forum reports.
OCuLink is cold-plug on most hosts (snippet). A Level1Techs-reported Windows 11 setup showed instability and 35-40% slowdowns.
A BIOS cap of the iGPU VRAM to 512MB was a forum workaround.
The MS-S1 MAX slot is x16 physical, x4 electrical, so an internal GPU gets the same link width.
No Windows-specific OCuLink driver documentation found; OCuLink exposes PCIe so the vendor GPU driver should apply (inference, not verified from a vendor page).
egpu.whenItHelps: Models that fit entirely in the eGPU's VRAM (documented: ~3x iGPU for an RTX 5080 16GB; 69-121 tok/s on a 96GB card), since only token-sized data crosses the link after load. Also a second device for image generation or small agents while the iGPU holds the big model (inference). Gaming tests put OCuLink loss vs a native slot in the single digits; the retailer's 2-3% inference-loss claim is unsourced.
egpu.whenItDoesNot: Models larger than eGPU VRAM or split across iGPU+eGPU: the link bottlenecks (1.6 tok/s overflow case). On Windows the dGPU+iGPU combination showed instability and 35-40% slowdowns in forum reports. No measured Stable Diffusion/Flux/video numbers over OCuLink or USB4 were found; model load time and any CPU/RAM offload are the link-bound parts (inference, not measured).

approaches.name: llama.cpp RPC
approaches.what: Layer-wise sharding across nodes over TCP; one head node, RPC servers on the others. Official docs call it proof-of-concept, fragile and insecure.
approaches.networkNeeds: Low bandwidth (a forum poster saw >20 MB/s use) but latency-sensitive.

measured.setup: 2x Ryzen AI Max+ 395, direct USB4 (~9.4 Gbps), Fedora 43

measured.result: tg ~8.25 tok/s, same as single node; Llama 405B 0.7 tok/s

approaches.maturity: Experimental; segfaults reported on some quants (Geerling). Fits larger models, does not speed them up.
approaches.windowsSupport: Not documented in the RPC README; all community Strix Halo cluster reports found are Linux.

approaches.name: vLLM + RCCL tensor parallel (kyuz0 toolbox)
approaches.what: Two-host TP=2 over Ethernet or RDMA/RoCE with a patched RCCL; the repo confirms both were tested on an Ubuntu 24.04 container. Patch details came from a search summary.
approaches.networkNeeds: AMD playbook: 10GbE switch, star topology. RDMA guide: Intel E810 100GbE via DAC in the x4 slot with a riser; RDMA latency ~5 us vs 0.07 ms Ethernet.

measured.result: No tok/s published. Latency 5.23 us (RDMA) vs 74 us (1GbE); bandwidth 50.6 Gbps.

approaches.maturity: Repo says benchmarks have not been run for the current image; AMD playbook gives no throughput.
approaches.windowsSupport: Linux only (Ubuntu container, Fedora host, apt in the playbook).

approaches.name: exo
approaches.networkNeeds: RDMA over Thunderbolt 5 only on macOS 26.2+.
approaches.maturity: README: Linux is CPU-only, GPU support under development; no AMD/Windows mention.

approaches.name: other: Minisforum published claim
approaches.what: Two MS-S1 MAX: 235B Q4 at 10.87 tok/s; four units ran DeepSeek-R1 671B Q4.
approaches.networkNeeds: Page does not state link, framework or runtime (10GbE ports and USB4 v2 are listed).
approaches.maturity: Vendor marketing, unverified; consistent with the 10-15 tok/s MoE range in community reports.

networking.measuredNotes: iperf3 2.35 Gb/s in one run. Search-summary of community data (underlying thread not opened): 1GbE cost ~13-15% on prompt processing, while 10GbE and 20Gbps USB cost 2-5%; token generation ~15% slower on every link.
Used for the 4-node test; no speedup.
MS-S1 MAX has 2 ports; the AMD vLLM playbook requires 10Gbps via switch. No tok/s comparison against 2.5GbE found on an opened page.
iperf3 TCP 8.85 Gb/s, ~0.5 ms ping, Soft-RoCE 4.3 Gb/s; Geerling got 10 Gbps; visorcraft ~9.4 Gbps effective. Latency-dominated, so extra bandwidth barely matters.
x4 slot caps it near 50 Gbps; RDMA latency 5.23 us.

limits: Clustering did not raise speed in Geerling's tests; it fit bigger models (ex-s11).
Latency, not bandwidth, limits layer-split clustering (ex-s07, ex-s08).
Tensor-parallel vLLM needs RDMA-class networking to pay off and is Linux-only (ex-s04, ex-s10).
MoE models run far faster than dense at this memory bandwidth (StarryHope: 235B MoE ~10-15 tok/s vs dense 235B ~3-5 tok/s, secondary estimate).
No documented Windows path for RPC, vLLM TP or exo on Strix Halo clusters.

options.name: Minisforum MS-S1 MAX (2U horizontal mount)
options.what: Desktop box that supports 2U rack mounting; 130W sustained/160W peak; 320W PSU; 2x 10GbE; x4 PCIe slot

options.name: Framework Desktop mini-rack (10-inch, 4 boards)
options.what: Four Ryzen AI Max+ 395 boards in a 10-inch rack (Computex demo per search summary); Geerling's 4-node build used 5GbE.

notes: Rack form factor is a mount, not extra performance; the interconnect is the same 10GbE/USB4 as a stack of desktops.
Framework boards draw 11W idle and ~150W peak per node (Geerling); at EUR 3,999 per 128GB MS-S1 MAX (EU shop), four nodes is ~EUR 16k before a switch (arithmetic).
Third-party MS-S1 MAX rack kits (USD ~69-71 on eBay) appeared only in a search snippet; not opened.
GPU rigs and workstation racks were not researched; gap.

footprints.example: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B 639MB, 4B 2.5GB, 8B 4.7GB (Ollama quants); 4B is BF16 on HF, up to 2560 dims
Qwen3-Reranker-4B has the same 4B parameter count as the embedder; size not opened, assume a few GB (estimate)
1M x 768d float32 = 5.72 GB (docs example uses replication 2); HNSW m=16 ~0.29 GB; 4-bit quantization ~0.72 GB. 1M x 1024d x 1 replica: ~4.1 GB by the same formula
10M x 1024d float32 = ~41 GB by the same formula, plus HNSW and payload; quantization reduces it
10M x 1536d = 57.2 GiB lower bound, add 15-50% headroom; 1M x 1536d ~5.7 GiB (arithmetic)
vector = 4 bytes/dim + 8; halfvec = 2 bytes/dim + 8. 1M x 1024d ~4.1 GB, 10M ~41 GB of vector data (arithmetic from README); HNSW graph and index size not published in README

rag.fitOnStrixHalo: 1M chunks fit easily on 64GB or 128GB beside a 4B embedder (~2.5GB quantized) and a reranker, at roughly 4-6GB of vector memory. 10M chunks at 1024-1536 dims need ~41-57+ GiB for full-precision in-RAM vectors by the vendors' formulas, which leaves little room for a large model on 64GB and a smaller one on 128GB; quantized or on-disk vectors (Qdrant 4-bit ~8x reduction in its example, pgvector halfvec 2x) are the realistic route. Fit is arithmetic from vendor formulas, not a measured co-run benchmark.
notes: Ingestion embedding competes with the chat model for the same unified memory bandwidth; no measurement found.
Qwen3-Embedding lets you choose 32-4096 dims (by model), so truncating to 512-768 cuts vector memory proportionally.
pgvector HNSW builds fast only if the graph fits maintenance_work_mem (README).

findings: Geerling (4 nodes): clustering did not accelerate inference, it only fit larger models; his advice was to scale vertically as much as possible.
Two-node llama.cpp RPC runs 139B-397B MoE models at 12-15 tok/s (USB4 ~9.4 Gbps), compared with single-node results of 42.7 tok/s (80B-A3B) and 86.1 tok/s (30B-A3B).
Latency, not bandwidth, limits layer-split clustering; token generation lost ~15% on every link per a community summary (not fully verified).
vLLM TP=2 on Strix Halo is documented but Linux-only and, for good latency, uses a 100GbE RDMA NIC in a x4 slot; no tok/s published.
An eGPU adds a fast lane for models that fit its VRAM (~3x iGPU in one source), but splitting across iGPU and eGPU is link-bound and a VRAM overflow is a cliff.
For a Windows-first buyer: every documented cluster setup (RPC, vLLM, exo) is Linux or macOS, and Windows dGPU+iGPU showed instability in forum reports.

gaps: No measured Stable Diffusion/Flux/video generation numbers over OCuLink or USB4 on Strix Halo or any mini PC were found.
No Windows 11 OCuLink driver documentation from AMD/NVIDIA/Microsoft was opened; the only Windows evidence is forum anecdotes.
Minisforum's network for the 10.87 tok/s claim is not stated; quant and framework not stated either.
DEG2 EUR price unverified (GBP 229 only); AG02 EU price is snippet-only; DEG1 snippets showed EUR 90 but only EUR 109 was opened.
The 1GbE/10GbE/USB prompt-processing percentages came from search summaries, not an opened page.
Qwen3-Reranker size and reranker memory not opened; pgvector index-size tables not in the primary README; no measured RAG-plus-agent co-run benchmark.
Racks: no price for a rack kit or Framework mini-rack opened; GPU-rig racks not covered.
MindStudio and EveZone are secondary/retailer sources; their eGPU numbers are unverified by a primary benchmark.
Windows support for llama.cpp RPC across Strix Halo nodes is undocumented in what was opened.
